newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Major CDMA vendors to develop digital tel standard.
newsitem.headline: Major CDMA vendors to develop digital tel standard.

text.p: Four telecommunication companies said on Wednesday they would work together to develop specifications for the next generation of wireless communication standards.

Lucent Technologies, Motorola, Northern Telecom (Nortel), and Qualcomm Inc said in a statement they would develop new standards to meet or exceed the current requirements for high-speed data transport to single subscribers.
A key aspect of the new specifications is that they would evolve from and be compatible with existing wireless systems which use code division multiple access (CDMA) technology, the companies said.
The new system would use wider-band CDMA technology to deliver advanced wireless services, including toll quality voice, high speed data, video and multi-media applications.
The statement said the four companies have contracts to provide commercial or trial CDMA systems in more than 25 countries.
The four companies said they expect the new specifications to achieve performance equal to or better than the performance of other proposals for new generation systems.
The first applications of the specifications are expected to go into commercial operation by the year 2000.
Operators in Japan, China, Latin America and the United States have expressed interest in the new technology, the companies' statement said.
The companies were in Singapore for a CDMA conference.
